A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 22 readable pages including Appendices A–E. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original monitoring experiments on coding tasks with adversarial side tasks, including detection results in Figures 3–9 and task-completion results in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their detection and task-completion results, including the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The monitoring procedures, attack policies, and fine-tuning method are unchanged. Both versions use the same hybrid score combining action-only and CoT scores with weight 0.55.

E1.justification: Both versions use BigCodeBench Instruct, the same eleven side tasks, and OpenCodeReasoning for fine-tuning. No datasets, tasks, or evaluation scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The same action-only and CoT monitors are compared with hybrid monitoring across the same models and attack policies. Comparator membership in the main and appendix comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The dataset partitions, successful-task filtering, five-attempt procedure, 1% false-positive calibration, model configurations, and fine-tuning budgets remain identical in Section 5 and Appendices A–D.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same analyses by task subtlety and attack policy, the false-positive-rate comparison in Appendix A.3, and the illustrative cases in Figure 2. No robustness or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: The plotted error bars and statistical reporting are identical. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including the appendix figures and completion tables. For example, Table 3 reports baseline DeepSeek-R1 completion rates of 30.3% at pass@1 and 44.0% at pass@5 in both versions.

T1.justification: The hybrid-score equation, threshold definitions, and task-subtlety criterion are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about CoT monitoring helping detect subtle sabotage, its vulnerability to misleading reasoning, and the benefits of hybrid monitoring.

C2.justification: The interpretations of monitor persuasion and complementary monitoring signals are unchanged. Section 7.4 retains the same limitations concerning single-step coding tasks, attack coverage, evaluation awareness, and deployment costs.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly provides a pointer to the project's cotredhanded/code GitHub repository. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, compute disclosures, and the Appendix E transcript link remain unchanged; this is additional code-access information.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and research positioning are unchanged. The additional acknowledgment does not introduce a cited study.

P1.justification: v2 adds the code-access sentence and Robert McCarthy to the acknowledgments, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause localized text wrapping and spacing adjustments on pages 6 and 10. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–6 retain the same displays and placement; there is no broader layout revision.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer in Section 5.2 modestly improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability, so the supported improvement is limited to clearer code-access information.
